steps.name: Renderer Module Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: Rendering setup and per-frame draw submission can be called through a renderer boundary instead of being directly organized as one monolithic rendering section in main.cpp, while existing Step 12 behavior remains unchanged.
steps.notes: Derived from the current architecture: Steps 4-10 established the OpenGL shader, VAO/VBO, texture, transform, and draw flow directly in main.cpp. Phase 3 then added text rendering using the same shader/render path. This step should separate renderer responsibilities without changing rendering behavior. Exact class/function design is intentionally not prescribed before implementation.
steps.implementation: Header-only pe::Renderer in src/renderer.h (513 lines): init/shutdown/clear/drawWorld/drawDigitString, owns shader program, uniform locations, world and text VAO/VBOs, and all five textures; destroyAll() replaces four duplicated cleanup chains. main.cpp 1675 -> 1082 lines (+115/-656). Zero CMakeLists.txt change. Known seams left inside for later steps: asset loading (14), camera/view math (15), UI digit path (21). Two disclosed deltas: audio cleanup on renderer-init failure path (leak fix, unreachable in normal play); blending toggles per drawDigitString call (visually identical).
steps.verification: In-place configure (524.0s) + Release build: zero errors/warnings in project code (pre-existing third-party C4244 in miniaudio.h unchanged); exe 1,171,456 bytes, fully static. Cyril ran build/Release/PureEngine.exe on 2026-08-15 and confirmed the full regression checklist: MENU/PLAYING/PAUSED/GAME_OVER, player movement, camera pan, three scenery (spin/tint/beep), three hostiles (chase/difficulty ramp/distinct Phase 5 textures), timer + high-score display, high-score persistence across relaunch.

steps.name: Resource Loading Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: Texture and other currently loaded render assets can be obtained through a small resource-loading boundary without changing the existing asset files or their visual result.
steps.notes: Derived from Step 10 and Phase 3. Current asset loading includes relative-path probing, stb_image loading, texture creation, and cleanup. This step should isolate ownership/loading responsibility before the project gains more assets. No resource cache or generalized asset database is required unless implementation proves it necessary.
steps.implementation: Header-only src/resources.h (116 lines): two free functions pe::loadRgbTexture and pe::loadRgbaTexture, relocated byte-compatible from pe::Renderer (Phase 5 RGB pattern and Phase 3 RGBA font-atlas block). Same 3-candidate CWD probe, same forced-channel stbi_load, same CLAMP_TO_EDGE + LINEAR sampling, same 0-on-failure contract. Ownership unchanged: renderer keeps and deletes all five texture names via destroyAll(); renderer.h contains zero stb_image calls. main.cpp changes comments/doc-block only. No cache or asset database per blueprint constraint. Zero CMake change. Commit 4bf7027 changed exactly: src/resources.h (new), src/renderer.h, src/main.cpp, README.md (+162/-67).
steps.verification: Incremental Release build against existing configured build/ (no deletion, no reconfigure): zero errors/warnings in project code; only main.cpp recompiled; exe 1,171,456 bytes, identical size to the verified Step 13 binary, fully static. steps.name: Camera Module Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: Camera position, movement, and view/projection calculation are handled through a camera boundary, while existing WASD camera movement and world rendering remain visually identical.
steps.notes: Step 6 introduced the camera math and Step 11 continued to store camera state directly in main.cpp/resetGame. This step separates camera responsibility from game-state and renderer code. Existing orthographic camera behavior must remain unchanged.
steps.implementation: Header-only src/camera.h (115 lines): pe::Camera owns position state (starts at origin), movement speed 3.0 units/s, reset(), move(directionX, directionY, deltaTime) applying axis += direction * speed * dt, view() via Mat4::lookAt(position, position + (0,0,-1), (0,1,0)), and projection() via once-built Mat4::orthographic(-6, 6, -4.5, 4.5, -1, 1). Architectural facts: camera state, movement, and view/projection calculation belong to the camera boundary; GLFW input polling remains in main.cpp (camera receives direction as data, zero GLFW code in camera.h); renderer drawWorld now receives the view matrix and performs no camera math; Step 16 input abstraction NOT started. main.cpp replaced cameraPos/cameraSpeed/projection locals with one pe::Camera; Step 14 resources.h untouched. Commit fff53c3 changed exactly: src/camera.h (new), src/main.cpp, src/renderer.h, README.md (+185/-54).

steps.name: Input Module Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: Keyboard polling and the existing edge-detection behavior can be accessed through an input boundary without changing the meaning of MENU, PLAYING, PAUSED, or GAME_OVER controls.
steps.notes: Step 3 established direct glfwGetKey polling and edge detection; Step 11 added state-dependent input meaning. The goal is separation, not a full action-mapping system. Existing controls must remain identical.
steps.implementation: Header-only src/input.h (107 lines): pe::Input constructed with the edge-tracked keys {GLFW_KEY_ESCAPE, GLFW_KEY_SPACE}; isDown() is the ONLY glfwGetKey call site in the codebase (level polling for ESC, SPACE, WASD, arrows); isEdge() is read-only against the previous-frame snapshot; update() is the snapshot's single writer, called once per frame after edge consumption — one edge per physical press, even while held. Architectural facts: keyboard polling and edge state belong to the input boundary; the entire state-specific meaning switch stays in main.cpp; glfwPollEvents and window lifecycle stay in main.cpp; raw GLFW key codes cross the boundary — no enum, no action-mapping system, no callbacks. main.cpp routes all level reads through pe::Input and replaces the old esc/spaceWasPressedLastFrame bookkeeping with input.update(window) at the exact former position; temporal order preserved (poll events, level + edge reads, state switch, snapshot update). Build fix during implementation: GLFW 3.3.8 glfwGetKey takes a non-const GLFWwindow*, so the boundary parameters are non-const. Commit 7749600 changed exactly: src/input.h (new), src/main.cpp, README.md (+190/-45).
steps.verification: Release build clean (incremental, no reconfigure): zero errors/warnings in project code; only main.cpp recompiled; exe 1,172,480 bytes. Architectural greps: glfwGetKey in code only in src/input.h; edge snapshot has a single writer; required temporal ordering confirmed by line-order inspection; no game meaning, deltaTime, or camera/player logic in input.h. Startup smoke test passed (window opened, full init, no crash). Cyril's manual physical-keyboard verification all PASS on 2026-08-15: SPACE starts from MENU once per press with no repeat while held, ESC pause/resume one edge per press, SPACE toggles clear color and navigates PAUSED/GAME_OVER to MENU, WASD camera pan and arrow-key player movement unchanged, ESC quits from MENU, no regression in timer/high score/textures/collision tint/beeps. The assistant performed the startup smoke test only and cannot provide physical keyboard input; all keyboard behavior was verified by Cyril personally. Push 24ca3ce..7749600 verified; six pre-existing untracked files untouched.

steps.name: Time/Timestep Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: Frame delta time is supplied through a timing boundary while preserving the existing deltaTime-driven movement, rotation, survival timer, and difficulty scaling behavior.
steps.notes: Step 2 introduced deltaTime, Step 12 uses it for survival time and hostile movement, and Phase 2 derives difficulty from survivalTime. This step isolates timing acquisition from gameplay calculations. No fixed timestep is prescribed.
steps.implementation: Header-only src/time.h (90 lines): pe::FrameTime owns ONLY the frame-time mechanism — the previous-timestamp state, start() seeding it pre-loop (the old lastFrameTime init), tick() reading glfwGetTime() once per frame, computing current-minus-previous, advancing the stored timestamp, and returning the delta through Step 11's shared float conversion relocated inside the boundary. Architectural facts: frame-time acquisition belongs to the time boundary (glfwGetTime exclusive to src/time.h, same containment Step 16 gives glfwGetKey to input.h); gameplay time meaning (survivalTime, difficulty scale, timer display, high score, PLAYING gate) stays in main.cpp. Critical invariant preserved: tick() is called at the same top-of-loop position the old code sampled, before glfwPollEvents, so each delta still spans the entire previous frame. No fixed timestep, accumulator, clamping, frame limiter, pause-aware timing, or elapsed-time API. Commit d598ffa changed exactly: src/time.h (new), src/main.cpp, README.md (+147/-29).
steps.verification: Release build passed (incremental, no reconfigure): zero errors/warnings in project code; only main.cpp recompiled; exe 1,172,480 bytes, identical size to the verified Step 16 binary. The assistant performed build, static checks, and the startup smoke test only and cannot provide physical keyboard input; all runtime behavior was verified by Cyril personally. Existing deltaTime behavior preserved end-to-end; no fixed timestep introduced. Push 2ea29a5..d598ffa verified; six pre-existing untracked files untouched.

steps.name: Entity Lifecycle Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: Entity creation/reset/removal responsibilities have an explicit boundary, while the current vector-based entity representation and reset behavior remain correct.
steps.notes: Step 7 established std::vector<pe::Entity> as the project's simple data-driven entity container. Step 12 and Phase 1 use push_back before the initialEntities snapshot. This step must not introduce a full ECS, registry, or component scheduler unless a concrete requirement appears.
steps.implementation: Header-only src/lifecycle.h (151 lines): free functions in namespace pe (the resources.h precedent), no class, no container ownership. buildInitialEntities() carries the six entity constructions relocated whole from main.cpp in identical order and values (order is contract: 0 = player, 1-2 = scenery, 3+ = hostiles chased at hostileSpeeds[h - 3] and textured by index); resetEntities(entities, snapshot) carries the snapshot-restoration assignment, the engine's only removal (it never erases or spawns at runtime, so no destruction or spawning machinery was invented); flagsForCount(count) carries the per-entity collision-flag sizing expression. Architectural facts: lifecycle operations belong to the boundary; the collections (entities, initialEntities, colliding) and all game meaning stay in main.cpp — resetGame() remains one atomic lambda at one call site now delegating only the entity restore and flag sizing, and hostileSpeeds[], the chase loop, the catch test, and texture selection are untouched. No ECS, no registry, no component scheduler, no manager. Commit aa9fae7 changed exactly: src/lifecycle.h (new), src/main.cpp, README.md (+201/-65).
steps.verification: Release build passed (incremental, no reconfigure): zero errors/warnings; exe 1,172,480 bytes, identical size to the Cyril-verified Step 16/17 binaries. Startup smoke test passed (window opened, full init, no crash). Static checks: the six construction values grep-verified byte-identical to the pre-Step-18 baseline in identical order; push_back removed from main.cpp code; the snapshot assignment exists only inside pe::resetEntities; resetGame() one atomic block at one call site; h = 3 / h - 3 / entities[0] index conventions intact; renderer receives the same vector in the same order via the unchanged drawWorld contract; all other source headers and CMake untouched. Cyril's manual runtime verification all PASS on 2026-08-15: all six entities at original positions (player 0, scenery 1-2, hostiles 3-5); rotation, chase speeds, difficulty ramp, collision tint, beeps, and catch to GAME_OVER unchanged; restart restores positions/rotations, camera home, timer 0.0 with no surviving run state; pause freezes with correct tint and resume continues; ESC quits, digits/textures unchanged, no visual corruption; high score survives relaunch. The assistant performed build, static checks, and the startup smoke test only and cannot provide physical keyboard input; all runtime behavior was verified by Cyril personally. Vector-based representation and reset behavior preserved exactly; no ECS introduced. Push e171535..aa9fae7 verified; six pre-existing untracked files untouched.

steps.name: Game State Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: MENU, PLAYING, PAUSED, and GAME_OVER state transitions and state-specific input/simulation rules are organized behind a game-state boundary without changing their current behavior.
steps.notes: Step 11 deliberately used one enum and one currentState variable instead of a state stack. Step 12 added GAME_OVER. This continuation should preserve that simple model unless the implementation exposes a concrete need for more structure.

steps.name: Audio Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: The existing miniaudio engine and four-slot sound pool can be triggered through an audio boundary while preserving collision-edge and GAME_OVER beep behavior.
steps.notes: Step 9 introduced miniaudio; Step 10 added per-entity collision edges and a four-slot pool. This step separates game events from direct miniaudio calls. It must not change the existing sound assets or trigger semantics.

steps.name: UI Rendering Boundary
steps.definition_of_done: The existing digit-only timer/high-score rendering can be invoked through a UI boundary while preserving screen-space behavior, formatting, placement, blending, and camera independence.
steps.notes: Phase 3 introduced the digit-only bitmap font and Phase 4 extracted drawDigitString(). This step recognizes the existing UI path as a separate responsibility without expanding the font system. No letters, menus, widgets, or general UI framework are required by this definition.

steps.name: World/Game Separation
steps.definition_of_done: The engine-facing systems and game-specific rules have a clearer boundary, while the current top-down survival loop still behaves identically.
steps.notes: Step 12 intentionally placed franchise-specific gameplay on top of engine systems, but much of the implementation remains in main.cpp. This step should separate responsibilities only where the existing code demonstrates a real boundary. It must not become a rewrite of the game.

steps.name: Engine/Game Integration Pass
steps.definition_of_done: The refactored engine boundaries and the current game can be built and run together with all previously verified gameplay behavior preserved.
steps.notes: Integration verification step. No new gameplay feature is required. The existing v1 loop, three hostiles, difficulty scaling, timer, high score persistence, state machine, collision feedback, audio, reset, and camera behavior are regression targets.

steps.name: Clean Build and Architecture Verification
steps.definition_of_done: A fresh clean build succeeds, the current game passes its regression checklist, and the resulting engine/game boundaries are documented without introducing unnecessary systems.
steps.notes: Final continuation checkpoint. The source material establishes fresh clean builds and direct verification as the project's existing standard. This step records the same discipline for the continuation rather than claiming a result before it happens.

kill_criteria: If any step's scope keeps expanding instead of shrinking, stop, cut scope, and re-record a smaller definition_of_done before continuing. Do not introduce an abstraction, manager, registry, or subsystem unless the current implementation demonstrates a concrete need for it.
